message.content:
Belts of heading 6217 (other made up clothing accessories) cover textile belts. HTSUS 6217.10 covers accessories, and 6217.10.95 covers other accessories of other textile materials. However, belts are often classified in 6217.10.9530 for those of man-made fibers, so I need to verify.

In CBP rulings, textile belts are usually classified under 6217.10.9530 (belts, of man-made fibers) or 6217.10.85 (containing 70% or more silk or silk waste, or of cotton). The alternative for belts of leather or composition leather is 4203.30. Here the outer layer is polyester webbing and the inner layer is polyurethane, which is plastic. Because the outer layer is textile and gives the belt its essential character, the belt falls under 6217.10.

Heading 6217.10.95 breaks down as follows:
- 6217.10.9510: Of cotton
- 6217.10.9520: Of wool
- 6217.10.9530: Of man-made fibers
- 6217.10.9540: Other

The belt is mostly polyester, so the man-made fiber subheading applies.
